Key Research Thinking Patterns: Ecological Momentary Assessment (EMA) for Temporal Dynamics: Utilizing Experience Sampling Method (ESM) and daily diary studies to capture within-person, time-sequential relationships rather than static cross-sectional associations. (e.g., Applying Latent Change Score (LCS) modeling in a 10-day ESM design to demonstrate the reciprocal, self-reinforcing cycle between daily job boredom and counterproductive work behavior.)

Mechanistic Mediation and Moderation Modeling: Employing advanced structural equation modeling and PROCESS macro analyses to identify specific affective and cognitive mechanisms linking distal job characteristics to proximal behaviors. (e.g., Testing moderated mediation models to show that job boredom fully mediates the link between perceived overqualification and extra-role behaviors, with career calling moderating the indirect effect on organizational citizenship behaviors.)

Rigorous Psychometric Scale Development: Following a multi-stage validation process involving Exploratory and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (EFA/CFA) across independent samples to ensure construct validity and predictive utility for new organizational constructs. (e.g., Developing a 25-item, six-factor scale for Attitudes Towards Artificial Intelligence at Work (AAAW) using three independent samples (N=2,841) to establish convergent and divergent validity for recruiting outcomes.)

Ecological Momentary Intervention (EMI) Design: Integrating real-time cognitive strategies with randomized controlled trials to test the causal efficacy of emotion regulation techniques on workplace performance and affect. (e.g., Implementing a three-week RCT with ESM to validate that situation-focused cognitive reappraisal is more effective than emotion-focused reappraisal in reducing negative affect and improving job performance, with effects persisting one month post-intervention.)
Summary Description: JeongJin Kim is an Industrial and Organizational Psychologist specializing in workplace affect, emotion regulation, and human-AI interaction. His research focuses on understanding the temporal dynamics of job boredom, perceived overqualification, and their impact on counterproductive work behavior (CWB) and well-being. Utilizing rigorous psychometric methods, he develops and validates scales for emerging constructs such as attitudes towards AI at work. Methodologically, he employs Experience Sampling Method (ESM), Latent Change Score modeling, and Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMI) to capture within-person processes and test causal mechanisms. His work bridges theoretical affective science with practical organizational interventions, demonstrating that real-time cognitive reappraisal strategies can effectively reduce negative affect and enhance job performance, offering actionable insights for improving employee retention, productivity, and workplace health.
